title: Answer before advancing, then lock it
statement: In an adaptive test, require an answer before moving on and lock it once given, since later items are chosen from it and going back breaks the selection.
detail: A reading assessment that follows an established adaptive test's documented interface locks each item once answered, with no back button, and keeps Next disabled until a response is given (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/MAP_PROXY_VALIDITY_CASE.md`). Its design-review procedure lists untimed, forward-only delivery among its hard constraints because back-navigation breaks the adaptive assumption (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/skill/SKILL.md`), each next item being the one most informative at the estimate the earlier answers set (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/01_PSYCHOMETRIC_DESIGN.md`).
against: The rule copies the reference test's conventions; nothing in these sources measured what allowing review would do to the scores.

evidence.quote: | C8 | **Untimed, forward-only** — power test, no clock; once answered, locked | NWEA confirmed: 3rd graders typically take 45–100 min; no time limit is set. Back-navigation breaks the adaptive assumption. |
- **Forward-only navigation**: once an item is answered, it is locked; no back button [NWEA-VERIFIED]
- **Answer-before-advance**: NEXT is disabled until a response is given
so that students experience familiar testing conventions and the official test measures reading rather than interface novelty
